The shape register $01FA keeps four bits and reads 0 (C75, the community claim; the data sheet text would read it back, a one-field reversal of its rmask to $000F). The tone coarse registers keep four bits (C60). The port registers $01FE and $01FF are plain stores in plan 05-04; what a read returns follows the direction bits and the pins from plan 05-05. Written by hand from data/psg/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.regmap.literal.txt; the psg-vectors step compares the two.

input.port_output_read.cite: none-found: no source read by the project gives the value a CPU read returns from a port whose direction is output
input.port_output_read.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: set each R7 direction bit, write a latch value, close a switch and read the port
input.port_output_read.revisit_trigger: a D10 port direction probe or a source for the output-mode read
input.port_output_read.note: A read of a port whose R7 direction bit says output returns the stored latch (low byte) and ignores the pins; no contention is modelled. The generator accepts only the value latch.

psg.mixer.port_dir_bits.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-207 (printed 5-26): bits B7 and B6 of R7 are the Input Enable cells of the two ports, the sense is not printed; the community page orders the two bits the other way
psg.mixer.port_dir_bits.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 port direction probe on owner hardware
psg.mixer.port_dir_bits.revisit_trigger: a primary data sheet of the console part or a D10 port direction probe
psg.mixer.port_dir_bits.note: A and B are the bit numbers of R7 that select the direction of port 0 ($01FE) and port 1 ($01FF); output is the bit value that makes a port an output. The port read consumes it through the generated psg parameters; the read path holds no bit number.

psg.clocks_per_step.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-207 (printed 5-26): the divide chains, the input clock by 16 and then by the period; a square wave toggles every half period, so one tone half-period is the period times 16 input clocks divided by 2
psg.clocks_per_step.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a tone of known period and compare the edge spacing with the profile
psg.clocks_per_step.revisit_trigger: when a primary source for the console part or a D10 tone capture exists
psg.clocks_per_step.note: One PSG step is 8 PSG chip clocks (16 master ticks, 4 CPU cycles on the NTSC profile): tone half-period P steps, noise shift every 2 NP steps, envelope step every 2 EP steps. Counters are integers; there is no accumulator. This corrects the earlier text of docs/time-base.md (D-09).

psg.sample_period_ticks.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a tone of known period and compare the edge spacing with the profile
psg.sample_period_ticks.note: Master ticks between two audio samples (one per PSG step, D-15). The generator refuses a value that is not ticks_per_psg_clock times psg.clocks_per_step.

psg.counter_model.cite: none-found: the data sheet prints the divide chain, not the counter structure
psg.counter_model.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: write a new period while a tone runs and capture the next edge
psg.counter_model.revisit_trigger: a die analysis, a schematic or a D10 capture of a period change mid-half-cycle
psg.counter_model.note: Each counter is empty at reset, reloaded from the effective period on its first step, counts down by one per step and fires at zero; a period write takes effect at the next reload (policy POL-PSG-02). The generator accepts only down-reload.

psg.period_zero.tone.cite: SRC-intv-wiki PSG (oldid 14940): a tone period of 0 acts as 4096
psg.period_zero.tone.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture the tone of period 0
psg.period_zero.tone.revisit_trigger: a primary data sheet of the console part or a D10 capture
psg.period_zero.tone.note: Effective tone period: value == 0 ? this field : value. Many other AY emulators treat 0 as 1 (C12).

psg.mixer.bits.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-207 (printed 5-26): the Enable cells of R7 with the active-low overbar; SRC-intv-wiki PSG (oldid 14940): bits 0..2 tone, bits 3..5 noise
psg.mixer.bits.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: a mixer register sweep against the sound output
psg.mixer.bits.revisit_trigger: a primary data sheet of the console part or a D10 capture
psg.mixer.bits.note: polarity 0 means a 0 bit enables the generator. The channel gate is (tone | tone_disabled) & (noise | noise_disabled), so a channel with both disabled is a constant 1. The tone and noise lists give the R7 bit of channel A, B, C.

psg.amp.env_select.cite: SRC-intv-wiki PSG (oldid 14940): the amplitude register bits 3..0 are the fixed level and the 2-bit select in bits 5..4 chooses the envelope scaled by a right shift
psg.amp.env_select.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: an envelope run through each select value
psg.amp.env_select.revisit_trigger: a primary data sheet of the console part or a D10 capture
psg.amp.env_select.note: fixed and select are [high bit, low bit] of their fields in the amplitude register; shift lists the right shift of the envelope level for select 1, 2, 3 (select 0 is the fixed level). The data sheet does not print the sense (C12).

psg.reset.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-205 (printed 5-24): a low reset pin resets all registers to zero; nothing else about the reset state is printed
psg.reset.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: read the registers and capture the first samples after power-on and after a console reset
psg.reset.revisit_trigger: a schematic of the reset line or a D10 capture
psg.reset.note: Registers zero, tone outputs 0, tone counters empty (reloaded on the first step), the noise register at its seed (psg.noise.lfsr) and the envelope held at level 0 until the first shape write (psg.envelope.shape_bits), both ports input.

psg.clock_phase_ticks.cite: none-found: no source gives the phase of the PSG clock against the master clock
psg.clock_phase_ticks.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a tone against the video timing
psg.clock_phase_ticks.revisit_trigger: a schematic or a D10 capture
psg.clock_phase_ticks.note: The PSG step grid starts at master tick 0 at reset (step k at k times the sample period). The generator accepts only 0.

psg.write_strobe_ticks.cite: none-found: no source gives the instant within a CPU cycle at which a register write takes effect
psg.write_strobe_ticks.resolving_evidence: test: psg.sample.write-effect-boundary and the psg.slice contract tests; a hardware reading is a D10 refinement
psg.write_strobe_ticks.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of a write against the sample edge
psg.write_strobe_ticks.note: Master ticks added to the start of the write's bus cycle to give the tick a PSG register write is stamped with; a sample at k times the sample period sees writes stamped below it (step first, then write, C78).

psg.max_unit_ticks.cite: derived from bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles (C53): (12 + 3 x 35) CPU cycles x ticks_per_cpu_cycle; the maximum unit on the real bus (wait 0) is 12 CPU cycles
psg.max_unit_ticks.resolving_evidence: test: psg.bounds.unit-ticks-max and psg.bounds.unit-ticks-real-bus (exhaustive probe through the CPU model)
psg.max_unit_ticks.revisit_trigger: when bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles changes or a stall unit can exceed U (the generator refuses bus.release_latency_cpu_cycles x ticks_per_cpu_cycle above U; stic.bounds.g-and-u-full-machine and stic.bounds.unit-ticks-le-U re-prove U with the bus windows live)
psg.max_unit_ticks.note: The proven maximum ticks of one CPU unit, published for the audio capacity slack (D-17): s = ceil(U / P) + 1. The generator refuses a value that is not (12 + 3 x bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles) x ticks_per_cpu_cycle.

psg.min_write_gap_ticks.cite: derived from the CP-1610 cycle table and ticks_per_cpu_cycle (C53): exhaustive probe psg.bounds.write-gap-min over every decle, SDBD off and on, waits 0, 1 and 35
psg.min_write_gap_ticks.resolving_evidence: test: psg.bounds.write-gap-min and psg.bounds.g-and-u (exhaustive probe through the CPU model, interrupt-entry units included)
psg.min_write_gap_ticks.revisit_trigger: when the CPU cycle table changes or a device other than the memory system or the STIC schedule of plan 06-08 can raise an interrupt or stall the bus (stic.bounds.g-and-u-full-machine re-proves the gap with the STIC lines live)
psg.min_write_gap_ticks.note: The minimum master ticks between two PSG register writes over ALL PSG-writing units, an interrupt-entry unit included: an MVO@ write at offset 4 of a 9-cycle unit followed by an interrupt-entry unit that writes at offset 2 gives 9 - 4 + 2 = 7 CPU cycles = 28 ticks. Instruction-only writers reach 9 CPU cycles = 36 ticks, the only density reachable by instructions alone; the published bound deliberately uses 28 so an interrupt source cannot silently break it. Phase 6 (plan 06-08) drives the VBLANK interrupt level and the bus-request windows: a bus-grant stall only lengthens the time between two writes, and stic.bounds.g-and-u-full-machine re-proves the gap through the full machine. The generator refuses a value that is not a whole number of CPU cycles.

psg.log_records_per_frame.cite: derived from psg.min_write_gap_ticks and psg.max_unit_ticks (C53): W_log = ceil(F / g) + ceil(U / g) + 1 = 2134 + 17 + 1; exhaustive probe psg.bounds.write-gap-min
psg.log_records_per_frame.resolving_evidence: test: psg.bounds.g-and-u (writes in T ticks <= (T + U) / g + 1 over every opcode x SDBD x wait in {0, limit}) and psg.buffers.worst-case-writer
psg.log_records_per_frame.revisit_trigger: when psg.min_write_gap_ticks, psg.max_unit_ticks or the nominal frame changes
psg.log_records_per_frame.note: Write-log records one frame slot is sized for: the capacity of a run is 16 bytes x this x (max(target - now, 0) / nominal_frame_ticks + 1). The generator refuses a value that is not ceil(F / g) + ceil(U / g) + 1 for the profile's frame F (scanlines x cycles per scanline x ticks per cycle = 59,736 ticks), g and U. Plan 06-08 re-proves the bound through the full machine with the STIC lines live: stic.bounds.log-records-per-frame-le-W measures the densest reachable writer (back-to-back non-interruptible MVO@ stores, never stalled by a bus window) at 1,660 records in a span of one frame, with the display on and off, below this value.

psg.period_zero.noise.cite: no source: the data sheet pages print a 5-bit noise period and no statement about a written 0 (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-207, printed 5-26); the tone and envelope rules of the same family act as the range top (SRC-intv-wiki PSG, oldid 14940), so the noise default follows by analogy
psg.period_zero.noise.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture noise-only audio with the noise period register written 0 and compare the shift spacing with 64 steps
psg.period_zero.noise.revisit_trigger: a primary data sheet of the console part or a D10 capture
psg.period_zero.noise.note: Effective noise period: value == 0 ? this field : value (the 5-bit register ranges 1..31, so 32 is the range top by analogy with the tone). A default by analogy, tagged as such; many other AY implementations treat 0 as 1 (C12).

psg.noise.steps_per_np.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-207 (printed 5-26): the noise frequency divide chain, the input clock by 16 and then by the 5-bit period; a shift register is clocked once per half period of that chain, so one shift every 2 NP steps of 8 chip clocks (inference)
psg.noise.steps_per_np.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a noise-only channel at two noise periods and compare the shift spacing with the profile
psg.noise.steps_per_np.revisit_trigger: when a primary source for the console part or a D10 noise capture exists
psg.noise.steps_per_np.note: PSG steps per noise period unit: the register shifts every this-many x NP steps (NP the effective noise period). Counters are integers; there is no accumulator.

psg.noise.lfsr.cite: no source for the console part: the data sheet defines a noise frequency but no register width, polynomial or seed (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-207, printed 5-26); the width, mask and seed are a project default chosen for the maximal period
psg.noise.lfsr.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a noise-only channel and compare the bit pattern with the profile LFSR
psg.noise.lfsr.revisit_trigger: a measurement (D10 noise capture) or a data sheet of the 8914-class part
psg.noise.lfsr.note: Right-shifting Galois register: if (s & 1) s = (s >> 1) ^ galois_mask else s >>= 1; the noise output bit is ((s >> out_bit) & 1) ^ invert. Mask $12000 with seed $00001 has the maximal period 131,071 (proved by psg.noise.lfsr-maximal-period). The alternative community mask $14000 is a one-field edit of galois_mask and has the non-maximal period 114,681 (tier 5 hint, SRC-intv-wiki PSG oldid 14940 names it, never a source of expected values). A zero seed locks the register, so the generator refuses it.

psg.period_zero.envelope.cite: SRC-intv-wiki PSG (oldid 14940): an envelope period of 0 acts as 65536
psg.period_zero.envelope.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture the envelope with the period registers written 0
psg.period_zero.envelope.revisit_trigger: a primary data sheet of the console part or a D10 capture
psg.period_zero.envelope.note: Effective envelope period: value == 0 ? this field : value, for the 16-bit period of the fine register at $01F3 and the coarse register at $01F7 (the wiki states 2 x 65536 PSG steps per state, which is steps_per_ep x 65536).

psg.envelope.steps_per_ep.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-207 and pdf-208 (printed 5-26 and 5-27): the envelope divide chain, the input clock by 256, then by the 16-bit period, and Fig. 3 names the period as the duration of one 16-state cycle; one state is 16 EP chip clocks, which is 2 EP steps of 8 chip clocks (inference)
psg.envelope.steps_per_ep.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture the envelope at two periods and compare the state spacing with the profile
psg.envelope.steps_per_ep.revisit_trigger: when a primary source for the console part or a D10 envelope capture exists
psg.envelope.steps_per_ep.note: PSG steps per envelope period unit: the envelope advances one of 16 states every this-many x EP steps (EP the effective envelope period), so one 16-state cycle is 256 EP chip clocks. The 16-state table is the engine's constant (the 32-step envelope is a different part, named in C12).

psg.envelope.shape_bits.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf-208 (printed 5-27): the sixteen shapes of Fig. 3 over the four shape bits; SRC-intv-wiki PSG (oldid 14940): the envelope is reset each time the shape register is written
psg.envelope.shape_bits.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture the envelope for each of the sixteen shapes and rewrite the shape register mid-cycle
psg.envelope.shape_bits.revisit_trigger: a primary data sheet of the console part or a D10 capture
psg.envelope.shape_bits.note: Bit numbers of the shape register (the four bits at $01FA): continue, attack, alternate and hold, and restart_on_write (1: a write to the shape register restarts the generator at its first level with an empty step counter; a period write never restarts it). C70 names the register address. After a reset the generator holds level 0 until the first shape write (psg.reset). Start level = attack ? 0 : 15; at the end of a 16-state cycle continue 0 holds level 0, continue 1 with hold 1 holds the last level (alternate 0) or the initial level of the finished cycle (alternate 1: shape 1011 holds 15, shape 1111 holds 0), continue 1 with hold 0 restarts at the initial level (alternate 0) or reverses direction (alternate 1).

psg.dac.levels.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog Fig. 9 axis labels as read in the Phase 5 discuss note (levels 15..9 printed: 1.0, 0.707, 0.5, 0.303, 0.25, 0.1515, 0.125 V normalised); the text for level 0 (0 V); levels 8..1 extrapolated by the printed halving every two levels. plan 05-01 could not obtain the reprint pages: the labels are not an independent source
psg.dac.levels.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner hardware: measure the analogue output voltage of each of the sixteen amplitude levels
psg.dac.levels.revisit_trigger: a measured DAC curve (D10) or a data sheet that prints the labels
psg.dac.levels.note: Sixteen unsigned integers in units of 1e-8 of full scale, indexed by the 4-bit level 0..15. Per-entry basis: levels 15 to 9 are the printed Fig. 9 labels, levels 8 to 1 are extrapolated (level n = level n+2 divided by 2: 8 from 10, 7 from 9, 6 from 8, 5 from 7, 4 from 6, 3 from 5, 2 from 4, 1 from 3 as derived in the discuss note), level 0 is 0 from the text. The printed 0.303 and 0.1515 V labels are not on a pure 3 dB ladder: [UNK] unresolved. The sum of three channels is at most 300,000,000 and fits uint32_t. THE CORE NEVER READS THIS FIELD (D-11): raw audio is the level indices; a test-side generator (cmake/IvsPsgProfileProbe.cmake) reads it for the psg.dac.* tests, and a wrong table cannot invalidate a raw audio golden.

stic.bus_bits.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) and SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 462: the STIC data bus is 14 bits wide (pins S00 to S013); bits 15 and 14 of a bus word are never driven by it
stic.bus_bits.note: Rule STIC-R02. The device kind memmap.device.stic14 (plan 06-06) refines the per-register masks of stic.regmap.

stic.regmap.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (STIC, oldid 15008) for the sixty-four addresses and the role of each range; SRC-intv-wiki (Memory Map, oldid 14847) for the readable and writable access column; SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) prints no register address (docs/stic/reference-notes.md, registers-printed: no)
stic.regmap.resolving_evidence: pending: a tier 1 to 3 STIC register description, or the Phase 7 reader diagnostic on owner hardware (D10 read-back of all 64 addresses)
stic.regmap.revisit_trigger: a primary register description, a D10 read-back or a Phase 7 reader diagnostic run on owner hardware
stic.regmap.note: One record per CPU address in ascending order $0000..$003F; name is the role of the literal, class is stored, strobe, collision or reserved. wmask: a store keeps value & wmask; rmask: a read gives (store & rmask) | (fill & ~rmask) with the undriven fill $FFFF, so rmask $0000 reads $FFFF and the collision rows read $FC00 | the stored bits (C81, C5). The stored widths and the bits above them are C86 (unknown-default-chosen, the literal rows carry the tier of each row: 32 stored, 8 collision, 2 strobe and 22 reserved rows). The collision clear-on-read is C87 (Phase 8). Transcribed by hand from data/stic/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.regmap.literal.txt, which stays the judge: plan 06-06 compares the two (stic.table.matches-literal).

stic.access_effects.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (STIC, oldid 15008): a write of $0020 enables the display for the frame, a write of $0021 selects Foreground/Background and a read of $0021 selects Color Stack; docs/stic/reference-notes.md rules STIC-R13 to STIC-R15
stic.access_effects.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-08 owner diagnostic with strobes at swept offsets and a frame capture
stic.access_effects.revisit_trigger: a D10 strobe sweep or a primary register description
stic.access_effects.note: Rows per register and access kind (a read is READ or FETCH, a write is WRITE or DW; every other register and access has no effect, collision clear-on-read is C87). The read of $0020 having no effect is unknown-default-chosen (STIC-R15, C82); the alias reads are C84 (stic.mode_select_addrs). Effects happen only if the register gate is open at the access stamp.

stic.mode_select_addrs.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (Memory Map, oldid 14847): the aliases of $0021 at $4021, $8021 and $C021 are sensitive to reads
stic.mode_select_addrs.resolving_evidence: test: stic.alias.* (plan 06-06) exercise the default and its reversal; measurement: a D10 read of the aliases with a known mode
stic.mode_select_addrs.revisit_trigger: a cartridge that legitimately maps data at $8021 or $C021 working on hardware, or a D10 alias read
stic.mode_select_addrs.note: The explicit effect decode of the mode switch, independent of the read-view region of the address (a read of $4021 decodes to cartridge space and the CPU receives the cartridge value). $0061 and the rest of $0040..$007F have no effect (unknown-default-chosen, C84). The generator refuses an address outside every memmap.region.stic_* range.

stic.alias_read_sensitive.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (Memory Map, oldid 14847): the aliases are sensitive to both reads and writes; docs/stic/reference-notes.md rule STIC-R16
stic.alias_read_sensitive.resolving_evidence: test: stic.alias.* (plan 06-06) exercise both values; measurement: a D10 alias read
stic.alias_read_sensitive.revisit_trigger: a cartridge that legitimately maps data at an alias address working on hardware, or a D10 alias read
stic.alias_read_sensitive.note: 1: a read of an address of stic.mode_select_addrs switches the mode; 0 disables the alias read effect (the register address $0021 itself always switches). Stored as a number because the profile schema has no boolean value type.

stic.power_on.cite: none-found: no source documents the STIC state at power-on (power_on_fill.stic holds the register contents); zero registers, Foreground/Background mode and a clear display latch are the chosen defaults
stic.power_on.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-09 owner power-on read-back and first frames
stic.power_on.revisit_trigger: a power-on read-back, a source that documents the state, or an owner EXEC run that depends on it
stic.power_on.note: registers is zero (the generator accepts only zero; power_on_fill.stic is the register fill), mode is fgbg or color-stack, display_latch is 0 or 1. The frame phase at power-on is stic.frame_phase_ticks (C90).

stic.backtab.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 199 (printed 5-18): the system RAM holds the background memory at 512 to 863 with the graphics words in the first 240; SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10): 20 x 12 cards, 240 background words of 14 bits
stic.backtab.note: Rules STIC-R03, CR-01, CR-02: the extent and the 14-bit use are printed; the word layouts are tier 4 (C96). The generator refuses a word count other than video.card_columns times video.card_rows.

stic.reg_window_cpu_cycles.cite: SRC-community-emu-docs: about 2000 CPU cycles after the VBLANK interrupt; SRC-intv-wiki gives about 2900 (the alternate)
stic.reg_window_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-06 owner probe of the window edges by cycle count with an original diagnostic
stic.reg_window_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 window probe, or a primary page that prints the window events
stic.reg_window_cpu_cycles.note: STIC register access window length from the frame start, in CPU cycles (alternate 2,900); the shorter figure is the conservative bound. Opens at FRAME_START and closes at REG_CLOSE (rules STIC-R18, STIC-R22). The mechanism (a pure function of the access stamp rather than the bus copy mode) is C83. Proven by tests to be followed, never to be right (D-02).

stic.gmem_window_cpu_cycles.cite: SRC-community-emu-docs: between about 3780 and 3790 CPU cycles; SRC-intv-wiki gives about 3796 (the alternate)
stic.gmem_window_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-06 owner probe of the window edges by cycle count with an original diagnostic
stic.gmem_window_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 window probe, or a primary page that prints the window events
stic.gmem_window_cpu_cycles.note: Graphics memory (GROM and GRAM) access window length from the frame start, in CPU cycles (alternate 3,796); the shorter figure is the conservative bound (rule STIC-R19). Closes at GMEM_CLOSE.

stic.irq_line.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (STIC, oldid 15008) and SRC-community-emu-docs: the vertical blank request drives the maskable interrupt line; the STIC wiring is not in the manufacturer catalog
stic.irq_line.resolving_evidence: test: stic.lines.* (plan 06-08) follow the profile field; measurement: a D10 line-edge probe
stic.irq_line.revisit_trigger: a schematic, a D10 line probe, or a primary page that prints the interrupt wiring
stic.irq_line.note: The CPU line the vertical blank request drives. The generator accepts only INTRM (the maskable interrupt request, a level; acceptance does not clear it, C41).

stic.irq_low_cpu_cycles.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (STIC, oldid 15008): the interrupt request is held for 3791 CPU cycles from the frame start; SRC-community-emu-docs gives 2907 and a commented 2920 (the alternates)
stic.irq_low_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 owner-gated probe by cycle count; affects whether a CPU can miss the interrupt
stic.irq_low_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 line probe or a primary source that prints the interrupt width
stic.irq_low_cpu_cycles.note: CPU cycles from the frame start for which INTRM is asserted (alternates 2,907 and 2,920); C91 records the line source and release. The generator refuses a width above the frame.

stic.frame_phase_ticks.cite: none-found: no source relates power-on to the frame; the first frame starts at machine time zero
stic.frame_phase_ticks.resolving_evidence: test: stic.profile.* (plan 06-06) perturb the field and follow the moved timeline; measurement: D10 power-on capture
stic.frame_phase_ticks.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of the first frame against power-on, or a source that documents the relation
stic.frame_phase_ticks.note: Master ticks from machine time zero to the first frame start S_0 (S_k = phase + k x F). A nonzero phase is allowed and means the interval before S_0 schedules nothing: the access gates stay open and no line is driven. The generator refuses a phase of F or more.

stic.bus.count.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) and SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 462: thirteen or fourteen second-sync requests per frame; thirteen is the chosen member of that set
stic.bus.count.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-07 owner bus-window probe of count, spacing and hold
stic.bus.count.revisit_trigger: a D10 bus-window probe or a primary page that prints the window train
stic.bus.count.note: Bus windows (BUSRQ pulses) per frame: windows 0..11 fetch card rows and window 12 fetches nothing in this model. Fourteen at the same pitch does not fit the frame; it needs a shifted start (the picture offset, Phase 8). C4 records the hold and the alternates.

stic.bus.first_start_cpu_cycles.cite: none-found: assumed equal to stic.irq_low_cpu_cycles (graphic time starts when the request ends)
stic.bus.first_start_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 bus-window probe or a primary page that prints the first window
stic.bus.first_start_cpu_cycles.note: CPU cycles from the frame start to the start of bus window 0.

stic.bus.pitch_cpu_cycles.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10): sixteen lines per card row (tier 1 text) times SRC-community-emu-docs 57 CPU cycles per line (cpu_cycles_per_scanline, C7)
stic.bus.pitch_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 bus-window probe or a change of cpu_cycles_per_scanline
stic.bus.pitch_cpu_cycles.note: CPU cycles between the starts of two bus windows: 16 lines x 57 cycles.

stic.bus.hold_cpu_cycles.cite: SRC-intv-wiki: the bus request is held for 114 CPU cycles; SRC-community-emu-docs gives 110, and 57 for the first window with 44 for the last (alternates)
stic.bus.hold_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-07 owner probe by cycle count
stic.bus.hold_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 bus-window probe or a primary page that prints the hold
stic.bus.hold_cpu_cycles.note: CPU cycles a bus window holds BUSRQ (alternates 110, the pair 57 and 44, and 114 with a 57-cycle acknowledge deadline). The generator refuses windows that overlap (pitch below hold).

stic.bus.rows.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) and SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 462: twelve card rows in the background
stic.bus.rows.note: Card rows fetched by the windows: window i fetches row i for i below this value. The generator refuses more rows than windows.

stic.bus.fetch_offset_cpu_cycles.cite: none-found: the row latch is taken one line after the window start by choice, equal to the acknowledge deadline of C4
stic.bus.fetch_offset_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: test: stic.steal.* (plan 06-08) exercise the latch instant; measurement: D10-VID-05 and D10-VID-07
stic.bus.fetch_offset_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 BACKTAB-write probe or a primary page that prints the fetch instant
stic.bus.fetch_offset_cpu_cycles.note: CPU cycles after a window start at which the card row is latched (ROW_FETCH). The generator refuses an offset above the hold.

stic.late_grant.cite: none-found: no source says what the STIC does when the CPU grants the bus late
stic.late_grant.resolving_evidence: test: stic.steal.* (plan 06-08) exercise late grants; measurement: D10-VID-07
stic.late_grant.revisit_trigger: a D10 bus trace of a late grant
stic.late_grant.note: Policy selector: the row latch is taken at its scheduled instant whether or not the grant has happened, and a late-grant counter is kept. The generator accepts only fetch-at-schedule, the one policy the engine implements.

stic.access_strobe_ticks.cite: none-found: no source gives the instant within a CPU cycle at which an access is tested against a window
stic.access_strobe_ticks.resolving_evidence: test: stic.window.* (plan 06-06) pin the default and its reversal
stic.access_strobe_ticks.note: Master ticks added to the start of an access to give the stamp that is tested against the windows.

stic.access_gating_when_off.cite: none-found: no source says whether the windows apply while the display latch is clear
stic.access_gating_when_off.resolving_evidence: test: stic.window.* (plan 06-06) pin the default; measurement: D10-VID-08
stic.access_gating_when_off.revisit_trigger: a D10 access probe with the display not enabled
stic.access_gating_when_off.note: Policy selector: the windows apply whatever the display latch is. The generator accepts only apply, the one policy the engine implements.

stic.video_slack_frames.cite: project rule D-15 (docs/stic/timing-notes.md, closed forms: capacity): a call completes at most floor(D / F) + 2 frame events because the largest unit U is below the frame F
stic.video_slack_frames.resolving_evidence: test: run.* capacity tests (plan 06-09) construct the corner now = E_k - 4, D = F - 1
stic.video_slack_frames.revisit_trigger: when psg.max_unit_ticks grows to the frame length or a device other than the memory system can stall the bus for longer
stic.video_slack_frames.note: The frames beyond floor(D / F) + 1 the output capacity rule reserves. The generator refuses a value other than ceil(U / F) with U = psg.max_unit_ticks (and refuses 2U >= F).

bus.line_sample_lag_cpu_cycles.cite: none-found: the machine layer samples the lines once per interruptible boundary at unit end minus one CPU cycle (POL-LINE-01)
bus.line_sample_lag_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: test: the Phase 2 interrupt boundary vectors and stic.lines.* (plan 06-08); measurement: D10 line-edge probe
bus.line_sample_lag_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: a D10 line-edge probe or a source that documents the sampling point
bus.line_sample_lag_cpu_cycles.note: Promotes POL-LINE-01 (C38) to a field: a unit that starts at tick b sees the levels of tick b minus this lag in CPU cycles.

video.card_columns.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) and SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 462: a background of 20 x 12 cards
video.card_columns.note: Cards per row of the background; the renderer produces this many columns and crops to the published width.

video.card_rows.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) and SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 462: a background of 20 x 12 cards

video.card_size_px.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10): cards of 8 x 8 picture elements
video.card_size_px.note: Picture elements of one card: width w and height h.

video.object_grid.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) and SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 462: the 167 x 105 object grid of which 159 x 96 positions are visible
video.object_grid.note: The nominal grid; consumed only by sanity checks (C105): the published width and height must fit inside it.

video.colors.note: Color indices 0..15; the display-off blank value must be outside this range of cut-off values.

video.last_card_column_px.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) and SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 462: the 20th card column is 7 picture elements wide; 159 of 167 positions are visible
video.last_card_column_px.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-01 owner capture of a card edge showing whether a 160th column is displayed
video.last_card_column_px.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of a card edge or a primary page that prints the 20th column
video.last_card_column_px.note: Width = (video.card_columns - 1) x video.card_size_px.w + this value = 159. The one-field reversal of C10 is 8, which gives 160 with no other edit (decision D8, D-12).

video.last_card_column_drop.cite: none-found: which 7 of the 8 pixels of a card in the 20th column are displayed is not printed; the right edge is clipped by choice
video.last_card_column_drop.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-02 owner capture of a card with markers in pixel 6 and pixel 7 of column 19
video.last_card_column_drop.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture or a primary page that prints the clipped side
video.last_card_column_drop.note: Policy selector: pixel 7 of every card of column 19 is not displayed. The generator accepts only right, the one policy the renderer implements.

video.row_lines.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 (printed 5-10) pdf 193 (printed 5-12): 96 display rows over 192 active lines, so two television lines per display row
video.row_lines.resolving_evidence: pending: Phase 8 border and delay rules, or a capture
video.row_lines.revisit_trigger: when Phase 8 models the border and the picture offset
video.row_lines.note: Television lines per display row; published as metadata, no pixel depends on it.

video.display_off_fill.cite: none-found: no source documents the output while the display is not enabled
video.display_off_fill.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-03 owner capture of the output while the display is not enabled
video.display_off_fill.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of a display-off frame
video.display_off_fill.note: Policy selector: a display-off frame is produced, flagged not displayed, with every position filled with the border color index. The generator accepts only border.

video.mob_field_origin.cite: SRC-community-emu-docs@programming-stic-object-field (rule STIC-R37): the object field starts 8 positions left of and 8 positions above the published plane; corroborated, not proved, by the printed 167 x 105 object grid against the 159 x 96 visible positions (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191)
video.mob_field_origin.resolving_evidence: measurement: a D10 capture of a MOB at X 1 and Y 1 showing which plane position the lower right pattern pixel takes
video.mob_field_origin.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of a MOB at the object-field corner or a primary page that prints the object-field origin
video.mob_field_origin.note: The offset in plane positions between the object field and the published plane: a MOB whose X coordinate is X puts its first pattern column on plane column X - x (and its Y coordinate Y puts its first pattern row on plane row Y - y). Each member is 0 to 15. One tier 4 lineage; no frame depends on a value other than 8.

video.mob_line_sample.cite: none-found: the lineage gives one television line per pattern row at the smallest Y size and a printed row of 2 lines, and does not say which line of a pair the published plane takes (rule STIC-R50)
video.mob_line_sample.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-14 owner capture of a half-height MOB line by line
video.mob_line_sample.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of a half-height MOB or a primary page that prints the Y size 0 behavior
video.mob_line_sample.note: Policy selector 0 or 1: the published plane row y shows television line 2 y + this value of the line-resolved MOB model (0 the even line, 1 the odd line). Only the two Y size codes that put two pattern rows into one plane row depend on it (frames F-M8 and F-M9, in-process tests only); the zooms 2x, 4x and 8x do not.

video.mob_prio_hides.cite: none-found: the lineage orders a MOB with the priority bit set behind the cards and does not say whether a card pixel that is off hides it (rule STIC-R43)
video.mob_prio_hides.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-11 owner capture of a MOB with the priority bit set against foreground and background card pixels
video.mob_prio_hides.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of a MOB with the priority bit set or a primary page that prints the priority ordering
video.mob_prio_hides.note: Policy selector 0 or 1: with 0 a MOB pixel whose MOB has the priority bit set is hidden only by a card on pixel (card foreground, colored squares colors 0 to 6) and shows through a card background pixel; with 1 it is hidden by every card pixel, so such a MOB is never shown. No frame, assert or marker depends on the case.

video.collision_x0_interacts.cite: none-found: the lineage says a MOB with X coordinate 0 is not displayed and says nothing about whether it interacts (rule STIC-R45)
video.collision_x0_interacts.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-10 owner capture of the collision registers with a MOB at X coordinate 0
video.collision_x0_interacts.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of the collision registers with a MOB at X coordinate 0 or a primary page that prints the rule
video.collision_x0_interacts.note: Policy selector 0 or 1: with 0 a MOB whose X coordinate is 0 does not take part in collision (no bit, from it or against it); with 1 it interacts at the position its X coordinate gives (plane column -8). No oracle row, frame or scenario depends on it: the collision scenario has no MOB at X coordinate 0.

video.collision_border_bit.cite: none-found: the lineage names a border bit (bit 9) of the collision registers and does not say which pixels set it (rule STIC-R45); the printed 167 x 105 object grid against the 159 x 96 visible positions (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191) is the only geometry
video.collision_border_bit.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-10 owner capture of the collision registers with a MOB at the plane edge and outside the plane
video.collision_border_bit.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of the collision registers with a MOB straddling the plane edge or a primary page that prints the border bit
video.collision_border_bit.note: Policy selector 0 or 1: with 1 a set pixel of an interacting MOB that lies inside the object grid and outside the published plane sets bit 9 of its collision register; with 0 bit 9 is never set. No oracle row depends on it: every rectangle of the collision scenario lies inside the plane.

video.collision_offscreen.cite: none-found: the lineage does not say whether MOBs collide where they are not displayed (rule STIC-R45)
video.collision_offscreen.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-10 owner capture of the collision registers with two MOBs overlapping outside the plane
video.collision_offscreen.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of two MOBs overlapping outside the published plane or a primary page that prints the rule
video.collision_offscreen.note: Policy selector 0 or 1: with 1 the MOB against MOB bits are evaluated over the whole object grid, including the positions left of, above and below the published plane; with 0 only over the published plane. No oracle row depends on it: no collision scene has a MOB outside the plane.

video.collision_display_off.cite: none-found: the lineage does not say whether collision is evaluated in a frame whose display is off (rule STIC-R45)
video.collision_display_off.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-10 owner capture of the collision registers in a frame with the display off
video.collision_display_off.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of the collision registers with the display disabled or a primary page that prints the rule
video.collision_display_off.note: Policy selector 0 or 1: with 0 a frame with the display off sets no collision bit and draws no MOB; with 1 the MOBs of such a frame are evaluated for collision against each other and against the border (there is no card layer in that frame). No oracle row depends on it: frame 0 of the collision scenario is not displayed and no row reads a bit set there.

video.border_ext_strip.cite: none-found: the lineage states the strip width of 8 plane positions for the left edge and draws, without printing the unit of the top strip, only the delay at its maximum (rule STIC-R49)
video.border_ext_strip.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10-VID-13 owner capture of the top strip height and of a strip with a nonzero delay
video.border_ext_strip.revisit_trigger: a D10 capture of a border-extension strip or a primary page that prints the strip units
video.border_ext_strip.note: The size of the two border-extension strips in plane positions: cols is the width of the left strip (extension bit 0) and rows the height of the top strip (extension bit 1). Each member is 1 to 15. The left strip width of 8 is the derivable core (rule STIC-R48); the top strip unit of 8 plane rows (a strip of 8 television lines would be 4 plane rows) is the pinned part (PD-8). Frames F-M4, F-M5 and F-M6 are derived under 8 by 8.

video.blank_value.cite: none: project pixel format D-13 (data/video/geometry.literal.txt, row not-displayed-sentinel): 0xFF marks a position that is not displayed
video.blank_value.revisit_trigger: when a host needs a different not-displayed marker or a frame format version is added
video.blank_value.note: The not-displayed sentinel of the index plane (IVS_PIXEL_BLANK). The generator refuses a value below video.colors.
